items.originalTitle: Oil Prices End Mixed as Traders Weigh Demand Outlook, Hormuz Shipping Risks
items.originalSummary: By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup Oil futures settled mixed Thursday with U.S. crude prices rising and international benchmark Brent slightly lower as traders weighed a weaker global demand outlook and signs of recovering Middle East crude supplies against persistent shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz. December Brent crude futures slipped 0.1% to $105.92 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate for December delivery rose 2.8% to $96.50 a barrel. The U.S. benchmark was buoyed by a large and unexpected draw in U.S. crude stockpiles for last week, and reports that the Trump administration is considering easing some sanctions on shadow fleets to increase tanker supply and lower the cost of moving crude. "This is more negative for Brent than for WTI," Price Futures Group senior market analyst Phil Flynn said in a note. "The elevated freight rates have been a major reason the Brent premium has stayed so wide. Any relief on tanker availability hits that premium directly." The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported an 8.6 million barrel withdrawal from U.S. commercial crude inventories last week, against expectations of a small stock build in a Wall Street Journal survey of analysts. U.S. crude production fell by 300,000 barrels a day as Hurricane Isaias shut in some offshore production in the Gulf of Mexico, which the U.S. calls the Gulf of America, while crude imports fell by 791,000 barrels a day. "The big stock decline may also be viewed as a one-off since all the decline developed within the Gulf coast region that was apparently affected more by Hurricane Isaias than widely expected," trading advisory firm Ritterbusch & Associates said in a note. Demand concerns are weighing on oil prices even as the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia continues to sustain a geopolitical risk premium, MUFG said in a note Thursday. The bank said shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains under threat following the sinking of two vessels. Shipping risks remained high after two Emirati cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday. Maritime security firms confirmed the losses, marking the first such incidents in months. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations separately issued warnings Wednesday about two container ships struck by unidentified projectiles while traveling across the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the continuing risks, Middle East crude exports have recovered substantially. The International Energy Agency said Wednesday that Persian Gulf crude shipments rose by 4.4 million barrels a day to 13.9 million barrels a day in September, reaching more than 75% of prewar levels. Global oil supply increased by 2.5 million barrels a day to 102.3 million barrels a day, driven by Gulf producers. However, the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping, the agency said. Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 10-15-26 1545ET

items.title: 交易商權衡需求前景和霍爾木茲航運風險，油價漲跌互現
items.originalTitle: Oil Prices Mixed as Traders Weigh Demand Outlook, Hormuz Shipping Risks
items.originalSummary: By Farhan Rafid and Anthony Harrup Oil futures were mixed Thursday with U.S. crude prices rising and international benchmark Brent slightly lower as traders weighed a weaker global demand outlook and signs of recovering Middle East crude supplies against persistent shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz. December Brent crude futures were off 0.2% at $105.84 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate for December delivery was gaining 2.6% to $96.37 a barrel. The U.S. benchmark was buoyed by a large and unexpected draw in U.S. crude stockpiles for last week, and reports that the Trump administration is considering easing some sanctions on shadow fleets to increase tanker supply and lower the cost of moving crude. "This is more negative for Brent than for WTI," Price Futures Group senior market analyst Phil Flynn said in a note. "The elevated freight rates have been a major reason the Brent premium has stayed so wide. Any relief on tanker availability hits that premium directly." The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported an 8.6 million barrel withdrawal from U.S. commercial crude inventories last week, against expectations of a small stock build in a Wall Street Journal survey of analysts. U.S. crude production fell by 300,000 barrels a day as Hurricane Isaias shut in some offshore production in the Gulf of Mexico, which the U.S. calls the Gulf of America, while crude imports fell by 791,000 barrels a day. Demand concerns are weighing on oil prices even as the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militia continues to sustain a geopolitical risk premium, MUFG said in a note Thursday. The bank said shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains under threat following the sinking of two vessels. Shipping risks remained high after two Emirati cargo ships sank near the Strait of Hormuz following attacks, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday. Maritime security firms confirmed the losses, marking the first such incidents in months. U.K. Maritime Trade Operations separately issued warnings Wednesday about two container ships struck by unidentified projectiles while traveling across the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the continuing risks, Middle East crude exports have recovered substantially. The International Energy Agency said Wednesday that Persian Gulf crude shipments rose by 4.4 million barrels a day to 13.9 million barrels a day in September, reaching more than 75% of prewar levels. Global oil supply increased by 2.5 million barrels a day to 102.3 million barrels a day, driven by Gulf producers. However, the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed attacks on energy infrastructure and shipping, the agency said. Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com and Anthony Harrup at anthony.harrup@wsj.com (END) Dow Jones Newswires 10-15-26 1348ET

items.title: 沃爾沃汽車與 NVIDIA 擴大合作夥伴關係以推動安全自動駕駛
items.originalTitle: Volvo Cars and NVIDIA Expand Partnership to Advance Safe Automated Driving
items.originalSummary: Volvo Cars today announced it is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA to unlock new levels of safety in automated driving technology in future cars from Volvo, building on the companies' decade-long collaboration. Guided by Volvo Cars' pioneering safety knowledge and powered by the NVIDIA Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, the technology will enable future Volvo cars to safely navigate complex real-world environments from door to door. This includes everything from highways and busy urban streets to parking scenarios. The technology will make its debut in a next-generation Volvo car as part of the company's recently announced largest-ever product push. Volvo Cars will combine its industry-leading vehicle safety systems and engineering expertise with NVIDIA's AI and accelerated computing technologies. These include the Hyperion sensor and compute architecture, Halos OS, and Alpamayo Stack driving software. Together, the companies will raise the bar for AI-enabled car safety while making driving feel easier and more effortless for customers, with a gradual introduction of eyes-off and mind-off driving. Volvo Cars brings nearly a century of real-world safety research and its human-centric approach to this development. The ambition is to set a new benchmark for automated driving that is safe, convenient and worthy of customer trust. "Volvo has been synonymous with car safety for almost 100 years," said Håkan Samuelsson, president and CEO of Volvo Cars. "By working with NVIDIA, we bring together two distinct strengths: industry-leading safety knowledge and world-class AI technology. That combination gives us a unique opportunity to create safer and more attractive cars for our customers." "Accelerated computing has transformed the car into an intelligent machine that can understand the world around it," said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. "Volvo has spent nearly a century protecting people on the road. Together, we're combining Volvo's extraordinary vehicle safety systems with NVIDIA Hyperion and Halos to build a new generation of cars that make driving safer and more effortless." historyItems.originalTitle: Department of Commerce Announces Agreement with GlobalFoundries to Amend Its Existing CHIPS Program Award and Reallocate $955 Million to Accelerate Investments in Silicon Photonics, Silicon-Germanium, and Advanced Packaging
historyItems.originalSummary: Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Office has agreed with GlobalFoundries to amend its existing award and reallocate up to $955 million in incentives under the CHIPS and Science Act. The amendment will increase the portion of an existing CHIPS Program award allocated to GlobalFoundries’ modernization and expansion of its semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Malta, NY and Burlington, VT. As part of the amendment, GlobalFoundries has agreed to expand its capital investment in these facilities to $5 billion. The total amount of the existing CHIPS Program award will not be increased. The investment will expand domestic manufacturing capacity for technologies increasingly critical to communications infrastructure and data centers, including silicon photonics, silicon-germanium and the first U.S.-based source of silicon interposers supporting advanced packaging technologies. “GlobalFoundries is expanding its investment to develop and manufacture critical semiconductor technologies enabling data center and high-performance compute infrastructure,” said Bill Frauenhofer, Executive Director for Semiconductor Innovation and Investment at the Department of Commerce. “The CHIPS Program award supports GlobalFoundries efforts to onshore and accelerate the development of these important semiconductor components." GlobalFoundries is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling technologies from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GlobalFoundries delivers differentiated, power efficient, and high-performance solutions for automotive, aerospace and defense, data center, smart mobile devices, internet of things and other high growth markets. historyItems.originalTitle: Chip-Machine Supplier ASML Boosts Guidance for Third Time on Surging AI Demand
historyItems.originalSummary: By Mauro Orru ASML Holding improved its annual forecasts for the third time this year and said it was looking at ways to boost production of its semiconductor-making machines even more as the race to build artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuels demand for advanced chips. The Dutch group is projecting annual sales between 44 billion euros and 45 billion euros, equivalent to a range of $49.27 billion to $50.39 billion, compared with prior guidance of 43 billion euros to 45 billion euros. Meanwhile, its gross margin--a closely watched metric of pricing power and profitability--should come in at roughly 56%, compared with a previous guidance range of 54% to 56%. The revisions show how much ASML's fortunes have come to benefit from the build-out of data centers that turned chips into a red-hot commodity. Surging semiconductor demand means that ASML's clients like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics and Intel will need more of its machines so they can produce enough chips. ASML shares in Amsterdam gained more than 2% in European morning trading, consolidating ASML's lead as Europe's most valuable listed company. Its stock is up more than 80% over the past 12 months on a wave of investor fervor around AI and expectations that chips and semiconductor-making tools will remain in high demand for years to come. "Our customers continue to increase their short- and medium-term equipment demand forecasts with us, driven primarily by their views on the size and duration of AI-related investments. In light of their demand visibility, some customers are expressing an interest in placing orders with us for 2029 and even 2030," ASML Chief Executive Christophe Fouquet said. AI demand pushed up the cost of certain types of chips as companies hoard semiconductors to power data centers, leading to a supply squeeze. Micron Technology Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said last month that supplies of memory and storage chips would be much tighter in the coming years. In a bid to cash in on that tightness, ASML is seeking to increase production of its deep ultraviolet lithography tools as well as its more advanced extreme ultraviolet systems. In July, it had earmarked a 30% boost in 2027 and another 30% in 2028. However, Fouquet said it was becoming clear that wouldn't be enough to meet demand and that ASML was looking at ways to bolster capacity even more, especially for 2028 and beyond. Earlier this year, ASML executives alluded to the possibility of price increases, saying that a tight chip market gave ASML more negotiating power. Finance chief Roger Dassen said that while the company had now completed conversations with key customers, the effect of higher prices wouldn't show on 2026 figures. "It will start to become visible partly in the course of 2027. The full impact of that you will start to see in 2028 and beyond," he said. ASML posted sales of 11.66 billion euros for the third quarter, up from 7.52 billion euros a year earlier. For investors, the near term has been choppy for Applied Materials, with the share price down 1.87% over the last session and 8.25% over the week. However, that pullback sits against a sharp year-to-date share price gain of 85.04% and a 1-year total shareholder return of 127.94%, which points to strong longer term momentum even as sentiment cools ahead of earnings and as the EPIC Center and recent AI-focused partnerships reset expectations around future opportunity and risk.

historyItems.summary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).
historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX Dragon Lifts Off for Thursday Cargo Delivery
historyItems.originalSummary: NEW YORK, October 13. /TASS/. The US company SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying the Cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station (ISS) on Tuesday. The launch was streamed on the website of the US National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The spacecraft lifted off from the spaceport at Cape Canaveral, Florida, at 06:33 a.m. local time (1:33 p.m. Moscow time/10:33 a.m. GMT) on the 35th resupply mission to the orbital station. Cargo Dragon will transport more than 2.8 tons of cargo to the orbiting outpost, including equipment for scientific experiments studying the effects of microgravity on heart tissue, as well as a set of solar arrays for the ISS. The spacecraft is expected to dock automatically with the ISS on October 15. In mid-November, Cargo Dragon is scheduled to return to Earth carrying the results of scientific experiments and equipment for repair.

historyItems.originalTitle: SpaceX stock poised for a catalyst-fueled 2027
historyItems.originalSummary: SpaceX ( SPCX ) isn't going quietly into what could be an eventful 2027. Elon Musk's rocket business said late last week it acquired a nationwide low-band spectrum portfolio . It positions Musk's satellite business, Starlink, to challenge legacy wireless giants across the US. Shares of AT&T ( T ), T-Mobile ( TMUS ), and Verizon ( VZ ) tanked on the news on Friday. Meanwhile, SpaceX is reportedly seeking to raise $40 billion in financing to purchase Nvidia chips. "The debate is whether a company this early in its public life should carry that much leverage," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said. "We think the contracted backlog in AI and the cash generation of Starlink give SpaceX the capacity to service it, and we would rather see this compute financed and deployed than deferred."

historyItems.originalTitle: Nokia to start dealing out GPUs in high-stakes AI-RAN gamble
historyItems.originalSummary: Some drivers are happy to run a car until the chassis has corroded and the engine coughs with every agonizing change of gear. Others less constrained by economic circumstances want a new vehicle every time the paint is nicked. Many big telcos currently seem to have more in common with the first group, determined to run their mobile networks until the basestations are shrouded in cobwebs. Any upgrades, including to 6G, should not have to require hardware replacement, they are telling vendors. Yet Nokia wants to sell them a completely new engine. The Finnish company has publicly teamed up with Nvidia to design radio access network (RAN) products built on the giant chipmaker's graphics processing units (GPUs). It has stopped developing new custom silicon with partner Marvell Technology, although it will continue to support its existing 4G and 5G range for years. Ultimately, however, customers will have to buy new hardware to enjoy new features. There is no guarantee the situation will be all that different for customers of Ericsson. Operators using its purpose-built 5G products today may need to invest in newer application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to support forthcoming 5G-Advanced and 6G software. But Nokia's GPU strategy is undoubtedly much riskier. While commonplace in data centers and certain gadgets, Nvidia's chips have never been used for RAN compute. If telcos balk at the idea, Nokia could be in trouble. "If you don't have a companion strategy that's based on classic ASICs, you really have created jeopardy, I think," said Marcus Weldon, a former Nokia chief technology officer who was also president of its Bell Labs research unit. Yet the rewards could be immense if Nokia can prove that GPUs have advantages over ASICs in the RAN. In recent months, it has argued that its GPU-led strategy will support a doubling in spectral efficiency, among other benefits, by 2028. In a RAN market that is not expected to grow in the next few years, such improvements could justify the initial hardware outlay and even translate into market share gains for Nokia, allowing it to recover 5G ground lost to Ericsson and Samsung. That could be a disaster for Nokia's rivals. Numerous operators are now giving Nokia's AI-RAN products a test drive before they become commercially available early next year. None has yet said anything in public about the initial experience, and many operators have previously voiced concern about using what is still perceived to be a very expensive and energy-hungry chip in the RAN. Overkill has been the word on some lips, as if putting a GPU in the RAN is like using a rocket launcher to kill a rat. But Nokia has been advertising a slimline GPU that could be slotted into an existing Airscale chassis originally designed to support Marvell Technology's silicon. It will have to function with the same power constraints and be available for the same price, according to executives. They have also promised it will support software upgrades and new AI algorithms for years – unlike any ASIC. The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. historyItems.originalTitle: Elon Musk's SpaceX just made a huge play to challenge the phone industry and stocks like AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are getting crushed
historyItems.originalSummary: Elon Musk’s SpaceX is moving past satellite internet, and it’s making a big move into the US wireless market. The company has agreed to buy cellular spectrum licences from investment firm Grain Management in a deal reportedly worth about $8 billion, its biggest move yet to compete with established mobile carriers such as AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, according to a WSJ report . The deal is for spectrum in the 800MHz band, which is for mobile services delivered via terrestrial infrastructure such as cell towers, not satellites. If the acquisition is approved, SpaceX could combine those airwaves with its growing Starlink satellite network to create a more comprehensive wireless service. SpaceX has already been rolling out Starlink in areas beyond the usual broadband. The company has been working with T-Mobile for over a year to offer basic wireless connectivity in remote areas. SpaceX is also launching newer Starlink satellites that are capable of carrying more data. The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to launch up to 15,000 satellites dedicated to mobile services. Leaders at OpenAI, Anthropic, and other AI companies are reportedly preparing for a potential AI disaster that could turn the public against artificial intelligence. According to an Axios report, industry leaders are privately running through possible scenarios for what happens after a catastrophic AI incident. What kind of AI disaster are companies preparing for? AI is a useful tool for handling many tasks in private as well as professional settings, but medical advice, especially diagnosis, is one area where I generally draw the line. General-purpose chatbots tend to sound confident and convincing while giving medical advice, even when they are wrong, as studies have previously found. That being said, Google's new research points to a much more convincing use for AI in healthcare. Its Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer chatbot, or AMIE for short, could help prepare both sides before the appointment even begins.

historyItems.summary: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) moved back into focus after the company and TELUS completed their first integration test connecting TELUS' terrestrial wireless network with AST SpaceMobile's satellite based system for direct smartphone to satellite service in Canada. AST SpaceMobile's integration progress with TELUS comes after a volatile run for the stock, with the share price falling 6.13% over the past day and 13.90% over the past month, contributing to a 31.80% decline in the year to date. Long term total shareholder return over three and five years remains very large compared with the initial listing period, suggesting recent weakness reflects shifting risk expectations rather than a simple reversal of the broader multi year move.

historyItems.originalTitle: NASA Sets Coverage for SpaceX 35th Station Resupply Launch, Arrival
historyItems.originalSummary: A SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft departs from the International Space Station on June 16 after undocking from the Harmony module's forward port. Dragon, packed with completed science experiments and cargo for retrieval and analysis on Earth, parachuted to a splashdown off the coast of southern California the following day.NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Tuesday, Oct. 13, for the next launch to deliver science investigations, supplies, and equipment, including the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, to the space station. This is the 35th SpaceX commercial resupply services mission to the orbital complex for NASA.NASA also will host a media teleconference on Thursday, Oct. 8 that will preview the cargo resupply flight, as well as provide a post-splashdown update for the agency's SpaceX Crew-12 mission, which will have returned to Earth from the space station Thursday morning.Loaded with more than 6,300 pounds of supplies, a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft on a Falcon 9 rocket will lift off from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Dragon will dock autonomously around 11 a.m. on Thursday, Oct. 15, to the space-facing port of the station's Harmony module.NASA's live launch and docking coverage will stream through a variety of platforms. Learn where to watch online:https://www.nasa.gov/liveIn addition to the solar arrays, the Dragon spacecraft will deliver hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity to help restore vision on Earth and 3D heart tissues models to advance large-scale drug testing on future missions. The spacecraft will carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and multiple sclerosis.The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart the orbiting laboratory and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.NASA's mission coverage is as follows (all times Eastern and subject to change based on real-time operations):Thursday, Oct. 81:15 p.m.: International Space Station briefing for Crew-12 return, and SpaceX's 35th Commercial Resupply Services launch with the following participants:Bill Spetch, deputy manager of Commercial, Low Earth Orbit ProgramDr. Liz Warren, deputy chief scientist, NASA's International Space Station OfficeLee Echerd, senior mission manager, Customer Operations and Integration, SpaceXAndreas Mogensen, leader, Human Exploration Group, ESA (European Space Agency)To participate in the teleconference, media must contact the NASA Johnson Space Center newsroom for call details by 12 p.m., Oct. 8, at: jsccommu@mail.nasa.gov or 281-483-5111. To ask questions, media must dial in no later than 10 minutes before the start of the call. historyItems.originalTitle: Judge could order Nebius to halt data center construction in Independence
historyItems.originalSummary: A motions hearing is set for Oct. 22 on a lawsuit related to the Nebius data center project in Independence.The Independence GUARD (Guardians United Against Reckless Development) Alliance filed the lawsuit to halt construction of the Nebius hyperscale AI data factory in the Little Blue Valley.Named in the lawsuit are the city of Independence, Missouri ADC Holdings LLC (data center developer) and Independence Power Partners LP.Residents along Bly Road in the Little Blue Valley are hoping to stop construction near their homes.The lawsuit alleges the city violated zoning and sunshine laws, as well as the city charter, and has failed to enforce city laws. Residents are asking a judge to pause the project.A hearing has been set for 9 a.m. on Oct. 22 on their motion for a temporary restraining order and the defendants' motion to dismiss.The Independence City Council approved billions of dollars in incentives for Dutch tech company Nebius to build and operate the 2.1-million-square-foot hyperscale AI data factory on 400 acres at the south end of Bly Road in March. Nebius broke ground on the first phase of the project in April.Nebius — which is party to the lawsuit through a subsidiary, Missouri ADC Holdings — provided us a statement about the lawsuit when it was filed earlier this year in Jackson County Circuit Court.“We are reviewing the claims and cannot comment on the case specifics,” Nebius Vice President of Public Affairs John Sutter said in a statement. “Nebius remains committed to complying with all applicable laws and regulations, and being a responsible partner for the community as our historic investment in Independence takes shape.”—

The letter can be downloaded here. In the third quarter, leadership among large growth stocks shifted from high-momentum semiconductor names to companies with clearer AI monetization paths. The ClearBridge Large Cap Growth Strategy outperformed its Russell 1000 Growth Index benchmark, benefiting from strong stock selection and disciplined valuation approaches. Despite volatility and a selloff in higher-beta AI stocks, the S&P 500 Index and NASDAQ Composite posted gains. The benchmark Russell 1000 Growth Index posted a modest gain of 0.9% while the Russell 1000 Value Index was up 2.6%. The Strategy broadened exposure across select semiconductor, AI infrastructure, and diversifying growth companies, while maintaining measured momentum exposure. The rebalance of the Russell 1000 Growth Index increased semiconductor weights and lowered software exposure, aligning with a thoughtful expansion into the AI and semiconductor infrastructure ecosystem. Overall, the strategy's focus on quality and valuation proved advantageous amidst market shifts. Also, check the fund's top five holdings to see its best picks in 2026.

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne enhances Titan HP for AI chip reliability tests
historyItems.originalSummary: Teradyne, Inc. announced a production-ready system that delivers enhanced burn-in capabilities on its Titan? HP platform. Traditional burn-in holds devices in banks of dedicated ovens at a controlled air temperature for hours before they move on to functional test.Teradyne Titan HP instead holds each device at its target junction temperature while running a realistic device workload, so reliability stress functions are optimized and thermal controls are enabled at the per-device level. Titan HP can be used for system level test or reliability testing, optimizing capital cost investments. For reliability testing, every device carries its full stress-and-test history on a single record.Per-site thermal control, tuned to each device's thermal and force zones, and paired with high per-device kilowatt power delivery, lets Titan HP sustain reliability-stress conditions on parts whose power draw and heat dissipation strain a conventional oven flow. The platform's asynchronous slot architecture loads and tests each slot independently, so a long stress run on one device does not idle the rest of the system, and individual sites can be serviced while the system continues to operate. Test programs run on the Teradyne Atlas software platform, which lets engineers import existing programs or build new ones and port them to other Teradyne system level test systems. Burn-in has long been standard for automotive and other high-reliability silicon.AI accelerators and cloud infrastructure devices are now entering the same category, driven by the high cost of a single failed accelerator in a deployed rack. Enhanced burn-in extends Teradyne?s test portfolio, which spans the AI device supply chain from wafer to data center.

historyItems.title: 摩根士丹利看漲 SpaceX 股價升至 6 月以來最高收盤價
historyItems.summary: After reaching highs in the initial days following its mid-June IPO, SpaceX SPCX shares fell sharply, declining about 48% through late July. However, since the start of August, the aerospace company's stock has turned the tables, rebounding about 58%. Morgan Stanley's MS bullish call on Sunday added to SPCX's momentum, with shares rising about 7.7% on Monday to their highest level since mid-June. SPCX rose about 0.40% during pre-market hours on Tuesday.

historyItems.originalTitle: Homeowners seek subpoena for mayor’s wife’s realty company in Nebius data center suit
historyItems.originalSummary: Birmingham Mayor Randall Woodfin is pushing back after his wife and her real-estate company were named in a discovery dispute tied to a lawsuit over a proposed Birmingham data center. In a statement posted to Facebook Wednesday, Woodfin said his wife, Kendra Woodfin, and her company, Iron City Premier Realty, had no involvement in the purchase or sale of the property where the Nebius data center is planned. “Here we go again,” Woodfin said. “This is a bald-faced lie. “My wife and her business had nothing to do with this property. She had no part in the purchase. No part in the sale. No connection to this litigation. There isn't a shred of evidence that says otherwise, because there's nothing to find. She wasn't involved. Period.” The comments follow an Oct. 6 filing in Jefferson County Circuit Court in which Iron City objected to a proposed subpoena from homeowners challenging the data-center project. Iron City said it “had no involvement” in the acquisition, purchase, sale, conveyance, financing, brokerage, development, zoning, permitting or closing of the property identified in the subpoena. The company also argued the subpoena is overly broad and that the plaintiffs have not established a factual basis connecting Iron City to the transaction. The court has not ruled on the objections. Woodfin also emphasized that his wife is a private citizen and has no role in Birmingham's zoning or permitting decisions. “She is a business owner. She is the mother of our children. She is a private citizen. She has never held office in this city. She doesn't vote on zoning. She doesn't sign permits. She doesn't sit on the Zoning Board of Adjustment or the City Council,” he said. Woodfin accused the attorneys behind the filing of intentionally putting his wife's business name into the case because of her relationship to him. “They wanted a headline,” he said. “Everybody knows how politically charged and unpopular data centers are. That's the play. You put a name in a court filing. Reporters read court filings. The story writes itself: ‘Mayor's wife named in data center lawsuit.’” Woodfin said he plans to pursue legal options to protect his wife's reputation. “We are going to be as aggressive as possible, exploring every legal recourse available to protect my wife's good name and the professional reputation of her business. This won't be the last you hear about it.” The mayor said he is accustomed to criticism but does not want his wife drawn into political disputes. “Come at me all day. I've been taking hits for nine years, and I'll take plenty more. That's the job I signed up for. My wife didn't. And I won't let her become collateral damage in a political hit designed to get at me.” The underlying lawsuit was filed by homeowners Robert B. Sansome and Gail Sansome against Hoar Construction LLC, Lakeshore Data Center LLC, Nebius Inc. and the City of Birmingham. The case remains in discovery, with a non-jury trial scheduled for March 8, 2027. A judge is scheduled to hear arguments Wednesday on objections involving subpoenas. The latest filings do not establish that Kendra Woodfin or Iron City Premier Realty participated in the property transactions at issue.

historyItems.originalTitle: Kratos Reports More Than $100M in Contracts for Space Intelligence Data
historyItems.originalSummary: SAN DIEGO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (Nasdaq: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, today announced multiple contract awards totaling over $100 million to develop prototype mission applications and cyber capabilities providing space intelligence data in support of joint operations across the space and cyberspace domains. Work under the contracts will provide warfighters with capabilities to collect and process complex radio frequency (RF) signals, develop intelligence on the operational environment and support the joint targeting cycle – the process used to identify, prioritize and target assets. The prototype systems will support electronic warfare and offensive cyber operations, including capabilities for access and battle damage assessment. The work leverages the KnownSpace ® Network, Kratos’ global RF collection infrastructure consisting of more than 190 strategically placed sensors around the world, along with RF data and capabilities provided by KnownSpace Recon+™, Kratos’ field-portable space domain awareness (SDA) terminals. In addition, the contracts will leverage Kratos’ software products, analytics and expertise in RF, signal processing, cybersecurity and software development, establishing a proven technology base that can be adapted and integrated to meet emerging space and cyber mission requirements. “Kratos brings decades of space experience together with proven commercial technology and agile engineering to solve some of today’s most complex mission challenges,” said Greg Caicedo, Senior Vice President at Kratos . “Our systems, software and hardware support missions across SDA, command & control, satellite operations and cybersecurity. By building on proven technology and rapidly adapting it to emerging mission needs, we can deliver new capabilities faster and keep pace as the space environment changes.” The Kratos KnownSpace family of SDA products and services which support these awards provide deep insights for global, sovereign, and tactical operations. Built on more than 30 years of satellite monitoring and RF expertise, the KnownSpace family combines global RF sensing, software, managed operations and deployable systems to detect, characterize and understand satellite and terrestrial activity. Solutions include enterprise software applications, portable form factors that can be deployed anywhere and persistent global RF signal monitoring and geolocation through its KnownSpace Network of over 20 locations and 190 sensors worldwide—the largest commercially owned, commercially operated (COCO) RF sensor network.

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Partners with Bright Machines to Put Robots, Test Tech in AI Infrastructure Microfactories
historyItems.originalSummary: NORTH READING, Mass. and SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER), a leading provider of automated test equipment and advanced robotics systems, and Bright Machines, Inc., a next-generation manufacturer bringing AI and data center infrastructure production to the edge, today announced a strategic investment by Teradyne in Bright Machines. The investment accompanies a strategic collaboration focused on integrating Teradyne robotics and test technologies with Bright Machines’ software-defined manufacturing platform and advancing AI infrastructure manufacturing. AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest electronics manufacturing buildouts in recent history. As hyperscalers, AI laboratories, silicon providers, and OEMs invest in next-generation compute, manufacturing has become a determinant of deployment speed, quality, and economic value, and manufacturers place a premium on lines that can be reconfigured in software as product designs refresh. Teradyne works with manufacturers across that ecosystem, including EMS and ODM providers, OEMs, and hyperscalers, supplying the robotics and test technologies that make high-mix, high-value electronics production possible. Bright Machines brings a unique software-defined manufacturing platform spanning design, robotics, automation, inspection, material movement, production intelligence, and operations, with a history of more than 130 microfactory deployments across 10+ countries and, today, active AI infrastructure production in the United States. "Physical AI is changing what is possible on the factory floor, and Teradyne and Bright Machines are partnering to accelerate this evolution," said Shantnu Sharma, chief development officer, Teradyne. "The combination of Bright Machines depth in software-defined manufacturing, and Teradyne’s decades of experience in robotics and test gives companies building AI infrastructure a faster path from design into production, with data behind every unit they build."

historyItems.originalTitle: Teradyne Makes Strategic Investment in Bright Machines to Advance AI Infrastructure Manufacturing
historyItems.originalSummary: NORTH READING, Mass. and SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Teradyne, Inc. (NASDAQ: TER), a leading provider of automated test equipment and advanced robotics systems, and Bright Machines, Inc., a next-generation manufacturer bringing AI and data center infrastructure production to the edge, today announced a strategic investment by Teradyne in Bright Machines. The investment accompanies a strategic collaboration focused on integrating Teradyne robotics and test technologies with Bright Machines’ software-defined manufacturing platform and advancing AI infrastructure manufacturing. AI infrastructure is driving one of the largest electronics manufacturing buildouts in recent history. As hyperscalers, AI laboratories, silicon providers, and OEMs invest in next-generation compute, manufacturing has become a determinant of deployment speed, quality, and economic value, and manufacturers place a premium on lines that can be reconfigured in software as product designs refresh. Teradyne works with manufacturers across that ecosystem, including EMS and ODM providers, OEMs, and hyperscalers, supplying the robotics and test technologies that make high-mix, high-value electronics production possible. Bright Machines brings a unique software-defined manufacturing platform spanning design, robotics, automation, inspection, material movement, production intelligence, and operations, with a history of more than 130 microfactory deployments across 10+ countries and, today, active AI infrastructure production in the United States. "Physical AI is changing what is possible on the factory floor, and Teradyne and Bright Machines are partnering to accelerate this evolution," said Shantnu Sharma, chief development officer, Teradyne. "The combination of Bright Machines depth in software-defined manufacturing, and Teradyne’s decades of experience in robotics and test gives companies building AI infrastructure a faster path from design into production, with data behind every unit they build."

Additional investor information can be accessed at http://www.axt.com.About AXT, Inc.AXT is a material science company that develops and manufactures high-performance compound and single element semiconductor substrate wafers comprising indium phosphide (InP), gallium arsenide (GaAs) and germanium (Ge). The company’s substrate wafers are used when a typical silicon substrate wafer cannot meet the performance requirements of a semiconductor or optoelectronic device. End markets include AI/data center connectivity, 5G infrastructure, passive optical networks, LED lighting, lasers, sensors, power amplifiers for wireless devices and satellite solar cells. AXT’s worldwide headquarters are in Fremont, California where the company maintains sales, administration and customer service functions. AXT has its Asia headquarters in Beijing, China and manufacturing facilities in three separate locations in China. In addition, as part of its supply chain strategy, the company has partial ownership in over ten companies in China producing raw materials for its manufacturing process. historyItems.originalTitle: Latest Injury Update on Texans WR Tank Dell Isn't Too Promising
historyItems.originalSummary: The wait for Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell continues. KPRC 2’s Aaron Wilson noted that it is currently “not the plan” to have Dell back following Week 4 against the Dallas Cowboys, the earliest he can return. Moreover, Wilson said Dell will not return “unless he can run at speed they want him to run at.” None of that is new from Wilson or the Texans. However, the insider did provide a rather dour outlook for Dell. “It is a serious injury, and he is not there yet, and they also don’t have a home for him at this point with the other receivers they have up. They’ve given us no timeline,” Wilson said during a live stream on October 2. “I’ve checked on this. It’s not imminent. I can tell you that. If it happens–if it happens–it’s later in the season.” Dell has not played since Week 16 of the 2024 season. https://twitter.com/Clay_HTXSports/status/2106128199990280418 He was a top target for Texans quarterback and draft classmate C.J. Stroud. However, the Texans have since added Kayshon Boutte (who replaces injured 2025 second-round pick Jayden Higgins in the lineup) and Jaylin Noel since Dell last played. They still have Nico Collins at the top of the pecking order. Bigger-bodied targets Xavier Hutchinson and Jared Wayne have also earned more opportunities in Dell’s absence. That is not to say any of them would play ahead of a fully healthy Dell. Part of his return process, though, will certainly include rebuilding the on-field chemistry and timing with Stroud and the offense. That is in addition to proving that he is still a superior option to some of his teammates in the passing game. Dell is also in the final year of his rookie contract. That only adds to the uncertainty around his future with the Texans. The former Houston Cougars star was supposed to play in the preseason, per DeMeco Ryans. “We’ve taken our time to kind of ramp them up slowly. So, our first week he was just on the side still, working, just some individual stuff with his position coach at the practice. And now, this past week, he got into routes on air. He got into group install. And yesterday, for the first time, he was able to get in the team drills,” Ryans said on SiriusXM NFL Radio in August. “We’ll keep giving him a little bit more every day. Planning for him to, hopefully, get out there preseason–in one of these preseason games coming up–and then be ready to go for the season.” https://twitter.com/JacobBarzilla/status/2078958050828755097 At the time, Ryans noted how proud he was of Dell’s comeback journey. For the situation to go from that sort of optimism to the more dour tones it has taken on now is disappointing. It is even more so given the kind of boost a healthy Dell could provide the 0-3 Texans. Instead, they will continue to bide their time without him. Meanwhile, he must continue working to prove he can be the same player he was for the Texans before his latest devastating injury two years ago.
